abstract: of 5-FU and cisplatin (CF) [1] . DCF therapy has shown a pathological complete response rate of 18.6%, significantly higher than the 2.2% observed with the CF regimen. Therefore, DCF therapy has become the standard preoperative treatment in Japan. However, it is also associated with a high risk of adverse events, particularly hematologic toxicity [2, 3] . A rare but serious life-threatening complication is the development of an esophagorespiratory fistula (ERF), which may result from direct tumor invasion or treatment-induced tissue injury [4] . ERFs occur in approximately 10-22% of patients undergoing chemoradiation therapy [5-8], but reports of ERF arising during chemotherapy without radiation remain limited. We report three cases of ERF that developed during neoadjuvant DCF therapy in patients with resectable or borderline resectable esophageal cancer.
